items.name: Cirro
items.title: Cirro: a site for water that feels as considered as the product
intro: Cirro sells packaged drinking water in India. The product already had a point of view: a 7-step purification process, sizes from 250ml to 2L, and certifications people can check. The site did not.
This is how I designed and shipped the marketing site so a first visit could answer one question: what makes this water different, and where do I get it?

blocks.label: Cirro
blocks.caption: The shipped homepage, from the hero through sizes and proof

blocks.title: The challenge
paragraphs: People landing on a water brand do not need a mood. They need to know it is safe, what size to buy, and whether the company is real. Those facts existed. They were just scattered across a story that started with adjectives.
The build had to make the product legible before it asked anyone to become a dealer.
blocks.quote: Tell me what makes this water different before you ask me to buy it.

blocks.title: Discovery
blocks.intro: I kept the first pass to four questions, so the page would have a job instead of a pile of sections.

items.title: What earns trust first?
items.body: Certifications and the purification process, named in plain language, ahead of the brand story.

items.title: What is the product, exactly?
items.body: Sizes as a set — 250ml, 500ml, 1L, and 2L — not a catalog hiding in a menu.

items.title: Who is the page for?
items.body: Someone choosing drinking water, and a dealer who needs a way to start a conversation.

items.title: What can wait?
items.body: The give-back story. It belongs after the product is understood, not instead of it.

blocks.title: Designing the page
paragraphs: One page, one argument. The hero states the product. Proof sits next: the purification steps, the certifications, the sizes. The story and the dealer path come after someone already knows what they are looking at.
I built it as a normal site, not a deck. The type stays quiet, the sections are short, and every block has to survive on a phone in one hand.

blocks.label: Sizes
blocks.caption: Sizes shown as a set, so choosing one does not take a second page

items.body: Product, proof, sizes, and a path to dealership live in one scroll.
250ml through 2L are visible without opening another screen.
The purification process is part of the page, not a footnote in a PDF.

blocks.title: Reflections
blocks.intro: A small marketing site still has to choose an order. This one taught me to be stricter about it.

items.title: Lead with the product
items.body: The story lands after someone knows what is being sold. Reversing that order makes the page feel like an ad.

items.title: Proof beats adjectives
items.body: A certification and a size do more than another sentence about purity.

items.title: Leave a real next step
items.body: Dealership is a different reader. They still need a door, even when the page is written for someone buying water.

blocks.text: Thanks for reading till the end!

notes.title: Notes
notes.description: Things I figured out while building — the tradeoffs behind a design, the checklist I wish I'd had, the lesson that only showed up after shipping.
